Turn: The spell effects expire at the beginning of the combat phase of the following turn. These spells are most commonly used to enhance a hero’s actions during the next turn. Permanent: The spell is permanent and never expires. Permanent spells can be in two states: active and inactive. When initially cast, the spell is active until the end of the action phase on the following turn and then becomes inactive. Place permanent spells face-up next to the hero board for the targeted hero or monster counter as a reminder. Once the spell becomes inactive, flip the card face-down, but leave it next to the targeted hero or monster. If the spell is broken, the spell card is returned to the caster to be cast again. Permanent spells may not be voluntarily broken nor revoked by the caster. Permanent spells are broken in one of three ways: • The target of the spell dies. • A Break Spells spell is cast on the target. • A hero in a civilization location may remove any number of permanent spells from a willing hero in the clearing for a cost of 5 gold per permanent spell dispelled. Active: When a permanent spell is active, the effects of the spell as described on the card apply. Inactive: When a permanent spell is inactive, its effects do not apply. The spell is inert. At any time, should the hero or monster under the effect of a permanent spell be in a map tile enchanted with the color of the banner of the spell card, the spell immediately becomes active again until the end of the action phase of the next turn. Flip the spell card face-up immediately. Permanent spells can become active immediately in one of three ways: • During the activation step of combat. • Being in a map tile enchanted with the matching magic color. • Being in a clearing with a source of colored magic from a treasure. Permanent Spell Example: An illusionist casts vapor form on herself during the game. Later, the illusionist moves into a clearing in a map tile that is enchanted with Gray magic. The illusionist instantly becomes vapor. The illusionist will continue to be vapor until the end of the action phase in which they are not in the presence of Gray magic at any point during their turn. Undead: Some spells are marked with an undead symbol. Undead are immune to these spells in all ways.

title: Missions
content: Missions are a great way for heroes to earn gold, legend points, and fame. Heroes may take missions from merchants during a trade action (see Trade action on page 12). A hero may keep two missions in their possession at the end of their turn. Heroes may discard missions at any time during their turn.

title: Mission Types
content: Missions are divided into 3 types: Atrocities, Expeditions, and Quests. Atrocities are more lucrative, but also make the hero an outlaw. Expeditions are a good way for a hero to earn more gold, especially the illegal ones. Quests are aligned to making the world safe for civilization and redeeming a hero that has become an outlaw. A hero may have a maximum of 2 uncompleted mission cards in their possession at the end of their turn. Discard any missions in excess. Mission cards may also be discarded face-up next to the mission card deck at any time during a hero’s turn. Discarding a mission sometimes has a mandatory reward and/or penalty as listed on the card.

title: Completing a Mission
content: To complete a mission, a hero performs the listed tasks and then spends a trade action as directed on the mission card. Requirements can be completed by a hero before the quest is accepted. In this case, the mission represents recognition of past achievements. The hero receives the gold, legend points, and fame shown on the bottom of the mission card. In addition to the mission rewards, the hero may receive additional variable rewards based on the bonus attribute of the mission. For each attribute symbol on the hero’s lineage and class card that matches the bonus symbol in the lower right corner of the mission card, the hero rolls one mission die. The mission dice show either fame or gold as additional rewards. The hero immediately receives the sum of all die roll results in addition to the listed rewards on the mission card. Some missions cause the hero to receive an outlaw token (example below). When completing a quest, the hero may discard one outlaw token they already possess. Quests do not allow a hero to discard an outlaw token they earn later. Upon completion, remove completed missions from the game. .

title: Completing a Mission Example
content: The human knight completes the temple defiler atrocity shown above. The bonus reward attribute for the temple defiler is cunning. The human knight has one cunning attribute (red arrows). The knight will roll 1 mission die and add the results of the die roll to the one legend point, 20 fame, and outlaw token earned for the atrocity.

title: Flying
content: Some monsters have the ability to fly and some game effects grant the ability to fly to heroes. Flying is already built into the maneuver speed on flying monster’s counters. Flying has no specific impact during combat unless mentioned in a spell or other game effect. Example: The spell, Fiery Chasm, kills all non-flying monsters and heroes that it hits. When a hero has the ability to fly, the hero may choose to fly during an explore or move action. Exception: A hero shape shifted into a flying monster must fly. • Each move costs 1 action regardless of terrain. • Flying heroes may move to an adjacent clearing via a path or, if not currently in a cave clearing, to any non-cave clearing in the current tile or a randomly determined, non-cave clearing in an adjacent tile. • Flying heroes may not take a hide reaction upon entering a clearing that already contains monsters.

title: Curses
content: Heroes can become cursed in a variety of ways. Curses are permanent unless removed via a treasure, break spells spell, or trade action at a civilization location. Mark curses by placing a pink status cube on the appropriate location on the back side of the reference card. Two of the curses are instant effects. Teleport sends the cursed hero to a random clearing on the map. Roll both summoning dice containing symbols and a d6 to determine location. Reroll any die rolls that do not match a revealed map tile. Summon causes wandering monsters to summon to the hero’s clearing. Roll the gray numbered die and summon that many wandering monsters for that terrain to the clearing, even in a civilization map tile. E.g.: giant bats could appear in the mine.

title: Outlaw Tokens
content: Outlaw tokens are the way that society marks the known thieves, ruffians, and renegades in Dragons Down. Heroes gain and lose outlaw tokens based upon whether they live within the laws of civilized society or not. If a hero has one or more outlaw tokens they are considered an outlaw. There is no limit to the number of outlaw tokens a hero may possess. Heroes receive one outlaw token as follows: • For each native they kill in the game. • Completing an atrocity mission as shown on the card (red banner). • Killing another hero that is not an outlaw (only allowed if playing with the optional Player vs. Player rules). Heroes may discard one outlaw token they already possess as follows: • Completing a quest mission as shown on the card (white banner). • Killing a hero that is an outlaw (only allowed if playing with the optional Player vs. Player rules). Outlaw tokens may impact your ability to haggle with merchants (see Haggling on page 21). During end game scoring or retirement, outlaw tokens may reduce the LPs and/ or fame of a hero prior to scoring (see Retirement on page 17).

title: Luring
content: During the challenge step in player order, prior to monsters challenging heroes, unhidden heroes may lure a single monster in the clearing. Monsters that are lured will challenge the hero that lures them. Once a monster is lured, it may not be lured by another hero. Monsters that are not lured will still challenge heroes randomly.

title: Tough Monsters
content: Monsters do not take wounds. If a single hit does not kill a monster, it does not harm the monster. This optional rule makes for a much more difficult game.

title: Closing the Distance
content: During the first round of combat, attack length, not attack speed, determines the order of attacks. Attack speed breaks attack length ties. Attacks still hit based on the attack speed compared to the maneuver speed and/or the results of rolling the hit dice. On all other combat rounds, order of attack is determined using attack speed.

title: Enchantment Limit
content: When casting a spell in an enchanted map tile, the spell caster ignores the rightmost solid-color spell box that matches the color of the enchantment rather than any spell box of their choice. This makes casting more powerful spells more difficult.

title: Wits Only
content: All heroes begin the game with 0 gold. Note that this impacts some hero classes more than others as all classes have different starting gold to account for the value of starting equipment and spells.

title: Shared Fame
content: The fame for killing monsters is shared by all heroes that wound the monster. Keep track of who placed which pink wound cubes on a monster. When the monster is killed, heroes receive the amount of fame in proportion to the number of cubes they placed up to the maximum health of the monster (including the death blow). Round down the amount of fame received by each player. Excess fame remaining is given to the hero that dealt the death blow.

title: Enchanted Paths
content: If a map tile is enchanted with a magic cube that matches the color of a hidden path in the map tile, the hidden path may be used freely as if it was a normal path. A hero using the hidden path does not automatically discover it. Hidden paths in enchanted map tiles may still be searched for by heroes.

title: Enchanted Realm
content: Whenever the wandering monster die shows a return arrow, in addition to returning monsters that are alone in map tiles to the monster tray, flip over all tiles that match the symbol rolled on the local monster die and place a magic cube matching the color of any hidden paths in the tile as if the tile had been enchanted by a hero normally. Remove any magic cube if there is already one present.

title: Endless Monsters
content: For players looking for an additional challenge, return monsters that are killed to the monster tray rather than placing them by your hero board. On future summoning results, the monsters may return to the game. Be sure to note the accomplishment in the adventure journal for future reference (mission completion, posterity, etc.). Natives and unique monsters are not returned to the monster tray (see the Monster Reference on page 26 for a complete list of unique monsters).

title: Red Meat
content: For players who wish to make armor even more valuable in the game, whenever a hero takes a non-fatal hit that does not strike armor, they must wound a heart.

title: Player vs Player
content: Heroes may block, challenge, and attack other unhidden heroes.

title: Hero Block Reaction
content: Trigger: Another hero has performed an action in the same clearing as the blocking hero, or the blocking hero is the active player. Heroes may become unhidden and blocked to attempt to block any number of unhidden, unblocked heroes in the same clearing during the action phase. Blocking is a reaction (does not count as an action) and follows all rules for monster blocking. Exception: An active hero may attempt to block heroes in the clearing, even if those heroes have not performed any actions yet. Targeted heroes may choose to take a hide reaction as normal to avoid being blocked.

title: Challenging
content: During the challenge step of combat, an unhidden hero may challenge one other unhidden hero by placing speed cubes in their maneuver box and placing their target token on that hero. During evasion, a hero may evade by exceeding the maneuver speed of all monsters and heroes challenging them. Challenging heroes may not evade this combat round. Any cubes placed in maneuver boxes during the challenge step by either hero must remain there for the entire combat round.

title: Aiming
content: When heroes target other heroes, players may choose to place one brown speed cube in one of the head or torso aim boxes on their own lineage card (but not both). This cube counts against the cube limit for the combat round. An aimed attack ignores armor that is not in the targeted location. Shields may always be used to block an aimed attack. Monsters do not aim and may not be aimed against.

title: Death Benefit
content: Should a hero kill another hero, the fame that normally would be discarded for a hero death is instead given to the hero that struck the death blow. Killing another hero may cause a hero to receive or discard one outlaw token per the outlaw rules.

title: Dwarf (Caver)
content: Dwarves are very comfortable in caves. Dwarves do not lose an action for spending any part of their turn in a cave clearing.

title: Elf (Magical)
content: Elves are raised around magic and begin the game with an extra spell from the hero starting spells deck. The selected spell must match the color of a magic cube they select for their hero.

title: Halfling (Stealthy)
content: Halflings are easily overlooked due to their short stature and quiet nature. Halflings may reroll one monster die per hide attempt, except during the cleanup step of combat.

title: Human (Adapted)
content: Humans are very comfortable in civilization locations and receive one additional free action during any turn they are in a civilization location.

title: Archer (Steady)
content: Archers have spent a lifetime honing their targeting skills. Archers may reroll one ranged attack die per attack.

title: Barbarian (Mountain Lore)
content: Barbarians grew up in the mountains. Barbarians may reroll one die during each search action performed in a mountain clearing.

title: Cleric (Divine Protection)
content: Clerics have the divine on their side. Any summoning die roll that would summon or move undead monsters to the cleric’s clearing may be rerolled once per turn. The new result applies only to the Cleric’s tile, with the prior result applying everywhere else.

title: Conjurer (Mastery)
content: Conjurers can control the random aspects of magic. Conjurers may reroll one die for the effects of a blue spell. Examples: Reroll one hit die for an Air Sword attack or each Tentacle attack. Reroll one die for Open Gate or Teleport. Must accept the new result.

title: Druid (Natural Emanation)
content: Druids know the magic of nature. Druids may choose not to wound green magic cubes in a spell box containing a wound symbol when casting spells.

title: Enchanter (Aura)
content: Enchanters are adept at enchanting the world. Enchanters enchant a tile using one action less than normal.

title: Illusionist (Focus)
content: Illusionists are extremely focused on their targets. When casting a spell with a “Target” or “Self or Other” symbol on it, the illusionist may choose not to wound a cube.

title: Knight (Health)
content: Knights are in excellent physical shape and skilled at dressing battlefield wounds. A knight may rest 1 cube for each rest action taken.

title: Rogue (Elusive)
content: Rogues are quick on their feet and hard to catch. When evading, rogues that tie the maneuver speed of the fastest challenger may roll the two hit dice and successfully evade on a hit or equal sign result. The rogue is blocked on a miss result. Rogues challenge other heroes normally.

title: Sorcerer (Specialized)
content: Sorcerers are adept at casting magic using one discipline. If a sorcerer casts a spell using only one color of magic cube, the attack speed of the spell is +1.

title: Warlock (Blood Lust)
content: Warlocks heal at the expense of others. Warlocks heal one cube each time the warlock hits an unarmored, non-undead enemy with a non- spell attack.

title: Warrior (Adept)
content: Warriors have great dexterity and coordination. During the adjust equipment step of combat, warriors may always unequip one weapon card and equip another weapon card.

title: Catacombs
content: Labyrinth: One side of the terrain pack setup card includes a labyrinth at the catacombs. Any loot attempt die result that is higher than the cunning attribute of the hero automatically fails, even if the loot roll would normally have resulted in a treasure being received.

title: Chamber
content: Massive Door: One side of the terrain pack setup card includes a massive door on the chamber. No hero may loot the chamber until it is opened. The chamber is opened by an attack upon it that causes 4 or more damage (including sword icons), by a hero possessing the skeleton key, or by a hero possessing 4 healthy might cubes when no monsters are present. Once opened, any hero may loot the chamber.

title: Secret Cache
content: When the secret cache is searched for and found by a hero, it does not need to be looted. The hero that first finds the secret cache immediately takes both the deep treasure and the gold as if they had performed a successful loot action. The hero receives the legend point and fame reward for finding a treasure site. If playing with the Dragons Down: Desolation expansion, the bandits can be summoned to multiple locations. The red arrow near the secret cache indicates that the chips for the bandits might be located on another setup card. The Bandits always summon as a group as if they were a single guardian. Hidden Trap: Side 2 of the terrain pack setup card includes a hidden trap on the secret cache. The hero that first finds the secret cache must wound one random cube or heart unless they possess the skeleton key treasure.

title: Shrine
content: Active Wraith: One side of the terrain pack setup card includes an active wraith at the shrine. After any loot attempt that results in a treasure being looted, immediately roll the local monster die. If it shows a treasure site symbol, the wraith is immediately summoned to the shrine from wherever it is located. Ignore all other results and monsters.

title: Unique Monsters
content: All Guardians, the Orc Lord, Orc Champion, Goblin King, and Kobold Rex are considered unique monsters. Unique monsters are immune to some game effects, such as being selected for the Shape Shift spell.

title: Demon
content: The Demon casts Fiery Chasm on the back side of the counter. If so, follow the rules of the Fiery Chasm spell as normal. Since the Demon is a flying monster, it is immune to the effects of the spell.

title: Dragons
content: The Great Drake, Great Wyrm, and Adult Dragons may breathe fire. Dragons breathing fire follow the characteristics of the Fireball spell (including targeting up to 4 heroes in the clearing). A dragon’s fireball is not a spell and is treated as a non-magical, ranged attack. Dragons will target up to 4 heroes in the clearing (determine randomly if more than 4 heroes are present). If only one hero is present, dragons will target only the one hero and the attack will be stronger per the spell.

title: Lich
content: The Lich casts Vapor Form on the back side of the counter. If so, the Lich casts it on their target, not on itself. The Lich may cast Vapor Form on a new target every combat round. Follow the rules of the Vapor Form spell as normal.

title: Titan
content: The Titan casts Teleport on the front side of the counter. If so, the Titan casts it on their target, not on itself. Follow the rules of the Teleport spell as normal. To determine the tile to which the target is teleported, roll both of the summoning dice to determine a terrain and a tile symbol. If either die roll is not in play, reroll that die until a tile in play is determined. Then roll a d6 to determine the clearing.

title: Adamantium Blade
content: Melee weapon. The optional might cube box on this card is automatically filled and does not count against the cube limit.

title: Alchemist’s mixture
content: One-time use. Permanently replace one color of magic cube with another color.

title: Artificer’s Concoction
content: One-time use. Ranged weapon.

title: Ascendant Ornament
content: Epic treasure. A purple magic cube placed on this treasure counts as a might cube on any might box on an active card of this hero. This card can have cubes placed on it in addition to other cards.

title: Band of Sagacity
content: Epic treasure. A yellow magic cube placed on this treasure allows the hero to reroll a hit die roll by or against them one time per combat round. This card can have cubes placed on it in addition to other cards.

title: Battle Staff
content: Melee weapon. The required might box on this card is automatically filled and does not count against the hero’s cube limit.

title: Bauble of Cunning
content: Increases the cunning attribute of the hero by one.

title: Bejeweled Breastplate
content: Armor. Valuable.

title: Bejeweled Helm
content: Armor. Valuable.

title: Bejeweled Shield
content: Armor. Valuable.

title: Belt of Expansion
content: Gain two additional miscellaneous positions in which to carry cards.

title: Belt of the Beast
content: Epic treasure. Receive one might cube while the treasure is equipped.

title: Bow of the Hunt
content: Epic treasure. Extra sharp. Ranged weapon.

title: Bracelets of Finesse
content: May place one red might cube from the hero’s healthy box in an attack speed or maneuver speed box. This cube counts against the combat round limit.

title: Bracers of Vigor
content: May place one brown speed cube from the hero’s healthy box in a might box. This cube counts against the combat round limit.

title: Broche of Deflection
content: One-time use. Cancel one hit against the equipped hero.

title: Cape of Alteration
content: Epic treasure. Healthy might cubes may only be placed in speed boxes. Healthy speed cubes may only be placed in might action boxes. Remember: Might cubes and boxes are red; speed cubes and boxes are brown.

title: Charismatic Gemstone
content: Increases the charisma attribute of the hero by one.

title: Clashing Ring
content: Placing a brown speed cube here increases the attack speed of the hero by one. This card can have cubes placed on it in addition to other cards.

title: Cursed Treasure
content: Instant. Draw a treasure card from the pool to replace this card (if the Cursed Treasure card is a deep treasure card, draw a deep treasure card from the pool). Then roll on the curse table to determine a curse that affects the hero. The curse occurs even if the hero simply viewed the treasure (e,g. merchant, treasure site, etc.). Then remove the Cursed Treasure card from the game. Multiple Cursed Treasures can be drawn in succession when replacing a Cursed Treasure.

title: Dagger of Bite
content: Melee and ranged weapon. Extra sharp.

title: Decimation
content: Epic treasure. A black magic cube may be placed on Decimation to increase the damage delivered.

title: Digger’s Ruin
content: May reroll one search die once per search action while in a cave clearing.

title: Disenchanter
content: While revealed, immediately remove any magic cube on the map tile containing the Disenchanter. Disenchanting does not flip the map tile over. The map tile in which the Disenchanter is located may not be enchanted for any reason. Must always be face-up. If face-down and viewed by a hero, it becomes active and is placed face-up (treasure pile, merchant, etc.). If its owner is killed, it is placed face-up in the clearing. Anyone entering the clearing immediately takes possession.

title: Dust of Destiny
content: One-time use. Reroll any one die or dice roll in which you are the active hero, the target, or the attacker.

title: Earthen Cincture
content: Epic treasure. Receive one green magic cube while the treasure is equipped.

title: Elemental Spherule
content: One-time use. Cubes may not be placed on other weapon or spell cards when using this card. When this attack is resolved, the spell, Elemental, is cast. No magic cubes are needed to cast this spell.

title: Elven Amulet
content: May reroll one search die once per search action while in a woods clearing.

title: Elven Slippers
content: Epic treasure. A green magic cube placed on this treasure increases maneuver speed by one. This card can have cubes placed on it in addition to other cards.

title: Enchanted Treasure
content: Instant. Draw a treasure card from the pool to replace this treasure, even if the hero simply viewed the treasure (e,g. merchant, treasure site, etc.). The map tile is flipped over and enchanted. Place a magic cube in the map tile matching the color of magic cube shown in the enchantment circle on the Enchanted Treasure card. Then remove the Enchanted Treasure card from the game.

title: Gage of the Thief
content: May reroll one loot die once per loot action.

title: Garb of the Gate
content: Epic treasure. May move to any revealed gate clearing paying normal movement costs as if connected by a path.

title: Gauntlets of Brawn
content: Counts as one might cube in an existing might box on a card. Does not add a might box to the card. This cube does not count against the combat round limit.

title: Gloves of Aggression
content: Counts as one brown speed cube in an existing attack speed box. Does not add an attack speed box. This cube does not count against the combat round limit.

title: Golden Icon
content: Epic treasure. Valuable.

title: Guard Charm
content: One-time use. May discard this treasure instead of taking one wound.

title: Hamblen’s Pendant
content: May reroll one search die once per search action while in a mountain clearing.

title: Hawkeye
content: May reroll one search die once per search action while in a plains clearing.

title: Horn of the Dark Angel
content: One-time use. Cubes may not be placed on other weapon or spell cards when using this card. When this attack is resolved, the spell, Fiery Chasm, is cast. No magic cubes are needed to cast this spell.

title: Icon of the Dragon
content: Epic treasure. Valuable. During monster activation, it summons as if a malevolent mountain summoning symbol (Juvenile Dragons) and a Sound summoning symbol (Adult Dragon) are printed on the map tile, if not already present. Printed summoning symbols on the map tile summon normally. If the malevolent mountain and sound summoning symbols are already printed on the map tile, dragons are not summoned twice. Must always be face-up. If face-down and viewed by a hero, it becomes active and is placed face-up (treasure pile, merchant, etc.). If its owner is killed, it is placed face- up in the clearing and anyone entering the clearing immediately takes possession.

title: Incanter’s Jewel
content: Epic treasure. Receive one blue magic cube while the treasure is equipped.

title: King’s Pardon
content: One-time use. When in a civilization location, the hero may discard up to two of their outlaw tokens. May not be used to discard other player’s outlaw tokens.

title: Mace of Smiting
content: Melee weapon. A required might box is automatically filled and does not count against the hero’s cube limit.

title: Magical Bowl of Mixing
content: Epic treasure. A blue magic cube placed on this treasure permanently converts a single magic cube from one color to another color, in either direction, as shown.

title: Mirror of Idolatry
content: Epic treasure. The hero may not sneak or alert while possessing this card. Must always be face-up. If face-down and viewed by a hero, it becomes active and is placed face-up (treasure pile, merchant, etc.). If its owner is killed, it is placed face- up in the clearing and anyone entering the clearing immediately takes possession.

title: Mithral Chainmail
content: Epic treasure. Armor. Cancels one sword. Lighter than normal chainmail.

title: Mithral Plate Armor
content: Epic treasure. Armor. Cancels one sword. Lighter than normal plate armor.

title: Mithral Shield
content: Epic treasure. Armor. Cancels one sword. Lighter than a normal shield.

title: Potion of Energy
content: One-time use. One additional speed cube from the healthy box may be played each combat round until the end of combat.

title: Potion of Flight
content: One-time use. Until the end of the next Action phase, this hero may fly.

title: Potion of Healing
content: One-time use. Move all cubes from the wounded box to the healthy box.

title: Potion of Maneuver
content: One-time use. Receive one brown speed cube permanently.

title: Potion of Might
content: One-time use. Receive one red might cube permanently.

title: Potion of Relief
content: One-time use. Remove all curses and permanent spell effects. May not be used to selectively remove curses and permanent spells.

title: Quick Ring
content: Placing a brown speed cube here increases the maneuver speed of the hero by one.

title: Ring of Malevolence
content: Epic treasure. Receive one black magic cube while the treasure is equipped.

title: Ring of Strength
content: The optional might box on one equipped weapon is automatically filled without using a might cube.

title: Ring of the Magi
content: Enchanting a tile requires one enchant action less to take effect.

title: Ring of Truth
content: Epic treasure. Receive one white magic cube while the treasure is equipped.

title: Robe of the Chanter
content: Epic treasure. Receive one yellow magic cube while the treasure is equipped.

title: Robust Ring
content: Receive +1 health while the treasure is equipped.

title: Satchel of a Giant
content: Instant. The hero draws and keeps two treasure cards (not deep treasure cards), then remove the Satchel of a Giant card from the game.

title: Scepter of the Sorcerer
content: Epic treasure. Receive one purple magic cube while the item is equipped.

title: Shadow Cloak
content: Epic treasure. Reroll any hide reaction once per turn. Must reroll all dice.

title: Shaman’s Kaftan
content: Epic treasure. Any magic cube placed on this treasure turns it into armor. If no magic cube is on the kaftan, then the kaftan is ignored and cannot be damaged. This card can have cubes placed on it in addition to other cards.

title: Shield of Defiance
content: Epic treasure. Armor. Armor value of 3. Weight of 2.

title: Shield of Mercy
content: Epic treasure. This treasure may be used as a normal shield. If a white magic cube is placed on this treasure during a combat round, the hero takes no wounds from any hits that are blocked by this shield, even if the shield is destroyed. This card can have cubes placed on it in addition to other cards.

title: Shoes of the Thief
content: May evade as if the hero had placed three maneuver cubes. No cubes are placed and no additional cubes may be added to make it faster.

title: Skeleton Key
content: Opens the monolith and chamber. Avoids hidden traps at the secret cache, hideout, and wrecked wagons.

title: Sparkler of Wisdom
content: Increases the wisdom attribute of the hero by one.

title: Spear of Piercing
content: Melee or ranged weapon. Extra sharp. If used two-handed, damage may be optionally increased by one.

title: Spell Book and Spell Scroll
content: Contains 1-3 spells. When a spell book or scroll is revealed, draw the indicated number of spell cards from the deck and place them face-down under the treasure card. A hero performing a trade action with a merchant may reveal the spell book to all players in order to draw and secretly look at the spells attached to the treasure card. The base price of the treasure card is the sum of the spells remaining with the spell book or spell scroll. The hero possessing the spell book or spell scroll may freely look at the attached spells at any time. These spells are available for a spell caster to learn if the hero has a magic cube matching the spell type. The treasure card is discarded if the last spell is removed from it, typically because a spell caster learned the spell.

title: Summoning Marcation
content: Epic treasure. Valuable. During monster activation, it summons as if all local monster die summoning icons printed on map tiles in adjacent tiles are also located in the map tile containing the summoning marcation. Must always be face-up. If face-down and viewed by a hero, it becomes active and is placed face-up (treasure pile, merchant, etc). If its owner is killed, it is placed face-up in the clearing. Anyone entering the clearing immediately takes possession.

title: Symbol of Alertness
content: May perform one alert action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Commerce
content: May perform one trade action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Greed
content: May perform one loot action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Knowledge
content: May perform one learn spells action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Magic
content: May perform one enchant action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Motion
content: May perform one move action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Rest
content: May perform one rest action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Stealth
content: May perform one sneak action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Symbol of Vision
content: May perform one search action which does not count against the turn’s action limit.

title: Talaria of the Gladiator
content: Counts as one brown speed cube in an existing maneuver speed box. Does not add a maneuver box. This cube does not count against the combat round limit.

title: Taper of Illumination
content: Epic Treasure. Do not lose an action when in a cave clearing on the hero’s turn.

title: Thief’s Lucky Coin
content: One-time use. Roll one die during one loot action.

title: Time Stone
content: One-time use. One attack in the clearing that ties on maneuver speed hits the target.

title: Tome of Conjuring
content: One-time use. Receive one blue magic cube permanently.

title: Tome of Fay
content: One-time use. Receive one yellow magic cube permanently.

title: Tome of Nature
content: One-time use. Receive one green magic cube permanently.

title: Tome of Power
content: One-time use. Receive one purple magic cube permanently.

title: Tome of Righteousness
content: One-time use. Receive one white magic cube permanently.

title: Tome of the Black Arts
content: One-time use. Receive one black magic cube permanently.

title: Tome of Tricks
content: One-time use. Receive one grey magic cube permanently.

title: Tome of Wizardry
content: One-time use. Receive one magic cube of the hero’s choice permanently.

title: Trickster’s Stone
content: Epic treasure. Receive one grey magic cube while the treasure is equipped.

title: Tricky Ring
content: Epic treasure. A grey magic cube placed on this treasure increases the hero’s attack speed by one. This card can have cubes placed on it in addition to other cards.

title: Vorpal Cutlass
content: Melee weapon. Extra sharp.

title: Wand of the Magician
content: Epic treasure. When casting targeted spells, may reroll one or two hit dice on each hit dice roll.

title: Warblade
content: Melee weapon. Requires that one speed cube be placed on this treasure in lieu of a might cube.

title: Writ of Redemption
content: One-time use. The price to buy any one card from a merchant is 1x the base price.

title: Universal Spells
content: Universal spells are accessible to all magic users and represent magic that requires no specific discipline of study. All casters of magic have access to spells from the universal arts.

title: Break Spells
content: Targeted. Instantaneous. Use any color(s) of cubes. Wound one cube. Immediately cancels all curses and spells on the target.

title: Black Spells
content: Black spells are from the realm of death and evil. Black spells tend to bring misfortune, curses, and death to those targeted by it. Black magic is not subtle.

title: Affliction
content: Targeted. Instantaneous. If the spell hits, the target immediately suffers one wound.

title: Curse
content: Targeted. Instantaneous. Wound one black cube. If the spell hits, the target receives one random curse from the curse table. The curse is permanent unless removed via the Break Spells spell or by paying to remove curses at a civilization location. Curses are not-cumulative, but a hero can have multiple curses.

title: Dark Matter
content: Targeted. Permanent. Wound one black cube. If the spell hits a monster or native, swap might and attack speed and ignore sword icons. If a monster is casting a spell, the new attack speed is equal to the number of spell boxes on the matching spell card and the monster attacks with might equal to the old attack speed. If the spell hits a player, might (red) cubes must be played on speed (brown) boxes and speed (brown) cubes must be played on might (red) boxes. Unresolved attacks swap speed and might cubes immediately as the targeted hero wishes, and may alter or cancel attacks. Example: not enough brown cubes to satisfy the mandatory might of a weapon.

title: Rule Undead
content: Targeted. Combat. Wound one black cube. If the spell hits, the targeted undead monster is controlled by the caster for the rest of combat, or until the caster is killed, targets the monster, or leaves the clearing. If the monster’s attack has not yet been resolved on the combat round in which the spell takes effect, the caster decides if the monster’s attack is canceled or continues. The caster receives all rewards for kills made by the controlled monster. The caster receives normal fame if the undead monster is killed by the caster.

title: Fiery Chasm
content: Instantaneous. Wound one Black cube. Attacks all unhidden, non-flying heroes and monsters in the clearing, including the caster. All targets that are hit by the fiery chasm are immediately killed and any possessions are removed from the game.

title: Blue Spells
content: Blue spells are from the realm of conjuring. Blue magic focuses on manifesting and controlling things in the real world. Blue spells tend to break the rules of the physical world for the caster.

title: Floating Disk
content: Self or other. Turn. The targeted hero may have any number of active treasures in their miscellaneous locations.

title: Open Gate
content: Targeted. Instantaneous. Wound one blue cube. If the spell hits, the target is placed in a random clearing containing a revealed gate.

title: Tentacles
content: Combat. Wound one blue cube. The caster places 4 tentacles on any number of targets, then roll the hit dice for each tentacle. Each double hit result lowers the target’s maneuver speed by one. Each single hit result lowers the target’s attack speed by one. Misses have no effect. Tentacles placed on dead targets may be placed elsewhere prior to the hero tactics step, otherwise they remain in place and the effects continue until the target is dead or the caster dies or leaves the clearing. Roll for the effect of newly placed tentacles immediately. If the caster is hidden, they must roll to stay hidden in any combat round that a tentacle is newly placed.

title: Air Sword
content: Combat. Wound one blue cube. Beginning next combat round, in addition to any spells or attacks the caster wishes to do in combat, the caster controls a sword with a might of 2 and 1 sword icon that attacks with a speed of 2 (attack length 6). The Air Sword may not be targeted and is immediately removed if the caster is killed or leaves the clearing. The caster receives all rewards for kills made by the Air Sword. If the caster is hidden, they must roll to stay hidden at the end of each combat round while the air sword is in play.

title: Teleport
content: Targeted. Instantaneous. Wound one blue cube. If the spell hits, the caster chooses a map tile up to two tiles away. Move the target to a random clearing on that tile.

title: Gray Spells
content: Gray spells are from the realm of trickery. Gray spells often involve altering the view of the world around the caster to confuse others, obfuscate reality, or making things disappear completely.

title: Divination
content: Self or other. Turn. The targeted hero may reroll any number of dice during one loot action.

title: Envenom
content: Self or other. Combat. Wound one gray cube. +1 sword icon to the next hit made by the envenomed hero or monster. If the hit target is not killed, it suffers +1 wound. Envenom affects the next hit regardless of whether it is made with a weapon, spell, or treasure. Envenom has no effect on the undead.

title: Illusion
content: Self or other. Combat. Wound one gray cube. All attackers targeting the hero or monster suffer -1 to their attack speed. The effect is not cumulative with other illusion spells.

title: Anti-Magic
content: Self or other. Combat. Wound one gray cube. The hero or monster may not be targeted by any spell with the target symbol on it. Indirect effects of spells without a target symbol may still affect the hero or monster. Anti-Magic does not affect the fireball of a dragon, but does affect other monsters that cast fireball.

title: Vapor Form
content: Targeted. Permanent. Wound one gray cube. If the spell hits, the hero or monster, and all possessions becomes vapor. All cubes are unavailable. All possessions are inactive (as if they were in the backpack). The target takes no part in combat. They may not block or be blocked. They may only perform the explore and move actions. They may use all hidden paths while in vapor form, even if not found. Used hidden paths are not found.

title: Green Spells
content: Green spells are from the realm of nature. Green magic seeks to live harmoniously with the natural world. Green magic calls upon the wild to aid the caster.

title: Nature’s Help
content: Self or other. Turn. The targeted hero may reroll any number of dice during one search action.

title: Trail Blaze
content: Self or other. Turn. Wound one green cube. The hero may move one clearing for each move action, regardless of the clearing type being entered.

title: Move Earth
content: Instantaneous. Wound one green cube. The caster may rotate the map tile they are in, or any adjacent map tile, to any orientation they wish. All paths on all tiles must always connect to other paths.

title: Calm
content: Targeted. Instantaneous. Wound one green cube. If the spell hits, the caster may return the monster to the appropriate monster tray location. The spell has no effect on heroes, guardians, or the undead.

title: Elemental
content: Combat. Wound one green cube. Randomly select one of the elemental counters and place it in the clearing. Starting next combat round, the elemental participates in combat under control of the caster. A caster earns no fame for killing their own elemental, but earns fame for kills made by the elemental. The spell expires if the elemental is killed. The spell expires if the elemental is killed, the spell caster is killed, or the spell caster leaves the clearing.

title: Purple Spells
content: Purple spells are from the realm of sorcery. Purple magic is about the raw power of magic calling upon sorcery to create energy and control it in the real world. Purple spells create, change, and destroy.

title: Iron Skin
content: Self or other. Combat. A hit against this target that does not strike armor follows the rules for armored monsters (removes one sword icon).

title: Strength
content: Self or other. Combat. Wound one purple cube. The target’s next hit during this combat phase causes +1 base damage. Strength spells are not cumulative.

title: Fly
content: Self or other. Turn. Wound one Purple cube. The hero can fly until the end of the action phase next turn (see Flying in the other rules section).

title: Fireball
content: Targeted (up to 4 targets). Ranged Attack. Instantaneous. Wound one Purple cube. Each target the spell individually hits is attacked by a separate ranged attack with a base damage of 2 + 1 sword. If only one target is selected, the spell has a base damage of 2 + 2 swords. Note: A dragon’s fireball is not a spell, but has the effect of a fireball.

title: Shape Shift
content: Self. Permanent. Wound one Purple cube. When this spell is cast the caster selects any non-undead, non-unique monster counter (no guardians or leaders. e.g. Kobold Rex) from the monster tray and replaces their hero with it. The caster may choose either side of the monster counter to be face-up during hero tactics each combat round and ignores the monster tactics step. The hero fights as a monster using the face-up monster characteristics, ignoring their own cubes and possessions. All monster wounds are healed at the end of combat. While Shape Shift is active, the hero may perform sneak, make noise, move, search, and loot actions. All cubes are unavailable. All possessions are inactive (as if in the backpack). Possessions gained while shape shifted are placed in the backpack. When inactive, place the monster counter near the target’s hero board. If the spell is canceled, return the monster to the appropriate monster tray location.

title: White Spells
content: White spells are from the realm of life and good. White spells tend to heal, promote life, and bring peace. White magic targets the undead as an abomination.

title: Soul Save
content: Self or other. Combat. Undead that attack this hero or monster must reroll the most favorable single hit die result rolled, unless both die results were blank.

title: Heal
content: Self or other. Combat. Wound one white cube. If the target is a hero, move any two cubes currently in the wounded box to the healthy box. If a monster, remove 2 wound cubes (pink cubes). May only be cast once per turn.

title: Life Armor
content: Self or other. Combat. Wound one white cube. If the target is a hero, they are protected by weightless armor of strength 2. The armor created by this spell must always be hit first by attacks on this target. It can be damaged and destroyed. It does not prevent wounds. If the target is a monster, it gains armored status.

title: Turn Undead
content: Instantaneous. Wound one white cube. All undead in the clearing are killed.

title: Peace
content: Instantaneous. Wound one white cube. Combat immediately ends in the clearing. Do not finish the combat round.

title: Yellow Spells
content: Yellow spells are from the realm of enchantment. Yellow spells tend to enchant, befuddle, and mesmerize. Yellow magic is subtle, but powerful for the caster who wields it well.

title: Hesitation
content: Targeted. Combat. If the spell hits, the target suffers -1 to their maneuver speed the next time this target is attacked. The spell expires immediately after resolving that attack. Hesitation is not cumulative with other hesitation spells.

title: Confuse
content: Targeted. Combat. Wound one yellow cube. If the spell hits, the target may not cast spells. Spells already cast are unaffected. If the target is casting a spell that has not yet been resolved this combat round, it is canceled.

title: Charm
content: Self or other. Turn. Wound one yellow cube. All attributes are +2 for all mission reward die rolls and haggle attempts.

title: Disorient
content: Targeted. Combat. Wound one yellow cube. Any unresolved attacks this round made by the target are canceled. The target may not attack in future combat rounds unless targeted or hit. Once targeted or hit, they may choose a target normally. The attack speed of the next attack performed by the target is at -2 speed. Disorient is not cumulative with other disorient spells.

title: Discord
content: Targeted (2 targets). Combat. Wound one yellow cube. The spell must hit two monsters in the same combat round to take effect. If the spell hits two monsters, cancel their current attacks this combat round. On future combat rounds, both monsters will challenge and target each other until one of them is dead or combat ends in the clearing. The caster does not control the monsters, so they are not targeted by other monsters. The caster earns fame for any kills made by these monsters while the spell is active. The spell expires if, at the end of a combat round, one or both monsters are killed.

title: Treasure and Item Banners
content: The banners on treasures and items show information as follows: Base Price: This is the price that a merchant will pay to purchase this card from a hero. This is also the base price used to calculate how much a merchant will charge to sell this card to a hero (the price is always base price x3) One-time Use: This card is removed from the game after use. One- time use cards may be used at any time during a player’s turn or in combat, even when first possessed without equipping. Cards with a combat effect may only be used in combat. Armor: This card is armor with an armor value as printed in the shield symbol. Armor is explained in the combat section of these rules. Weight: This card requires that a hero has a number of healthy might cubes equal to the number shown. If not at any time, the card is immediately unequipped to the hero’s backpack (see Equipping in Other Rules). Attack Length: If two attacks have the same attack speed, weapons and spells with higher numbers are resolved before lower numbers. Some weapons have two numbers. See Melee or Ranged below. Melee: This card is a melee weapon. Ranged: This card is a ranged weapon. If it hits, roll the ranged attack dice to modify the effects of the attack as described in the combat section of these rules. Melee or Ranged: This weapon may be used as a melee or a ranged weapon. If used as a melee weapon, use the top attack length. If used as a ranged weapon (thrown), use the bottom attack length. Weapons may only be thrown with one hand. When thrown, they are placed to the side of the hero board. Thrown weapons are removed from the game permanently if all monsters are not killed during combat this turn. Permanent: The effects of this magic item last for the entire game. Combat: The effects of this treasure last for the duration of the combat. Once combat is over, the effects are terminated. Position Neck: This card is placed on the hero’s neck when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Position Waist: This card is placed on the hero’s waist when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Position Feet: This card is placed on the hero’s feet when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Position Head: This card is placed on the hero’s head when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Position Chest: This card is placed on the hero’s chest when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Position Head and Chest: This card is placed on the hero’s head and chest when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Place the card on the white dotted lined area that covers both locations. Neither location is available for other cards. Position One-handed Weapon: This card is placed on one of the hero’s weapon locations (does not matter which one) when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). A hero may not have two weapons active, even if both are one-handed weapons. Position Two-handed Weapon: This card is placed on both of the hero’s weapon locations when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Place the card on the white dotted lined area that covers both locations. Neither location is available for other cards. Spears may be wielded with one or two-hands. The optional might box is only available if using two hands. Position Single Hand: This card is placed on one of the hero’s hand locations (does not matter which one) when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Position Two Hands: This card is placed on both of the hero’s hand locations when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Place the card on the white dotted lined area that covers both locations. Neither location is available for other cards. Position Miscellaneous: This card is placed on one of the hero’s miscellaneous locations (does not matter which one) when active (and face-down in the backpack when inactive). Position Backpack: Cards may always be placed in the backpack. Cards placed in the backpack are face-down, inactive, hidden from other players, and need not be revealed. Position Backpack Special: This card must always be face-up. If face- down and viewed by a hero, it becomes active and is placed face-up (treasure pile, merchant, etc.). If its owner is killed, it is placed face-up in the clearing. Anyone entering the clearing immediately takes possession of the card. Instantaneous: The effects of this treasure occur immediately. The treasure is then removed from the game.

title: Spells
content: Price: The base price of the spell card. Spell cards cannot be bought or sold unless attached to a spell book or spell scroll. When a hero buys or sells a spell book or spell scroll, all spells remain attached to the treasure card. The base price of a spell book or spell scroll is the sum of all spells attached to the treasure card. Targeted: This spell must be targeted at the caster or a single target in the clearing with the caster. If there is a number in the target symbol, the caster may target up to that many targets. The spell only takes effect if the spell hits using normal attack rules. A hero may voluntarily accept a hit from a targeted spell when cast. Self or other: This spell may be cast on self, another hero, or a monster in the same clearing as the caster. The spell does not need to hit to take effect. Self: This spell targets the caster and automatically takes effect when cast. Melee: The casting of this spell acts like a melee weapon. If it hits, treat it like a melee weapon attack per the explanation on the card. Ranged: The casting of this spell acts like a ranged weapon. If it hits, roll the ranged attack dice to modify the effects of the attack as normal. Instantaneous: The spell occurs instantly and then expires. Combat: The spell lasts for the duration of combat, until the caster or target is killed or evades. Then the spell expires. Turn: The spell effects expire at the beginning of the combat phase of the following turn. These spells are most commonly used to enhance a hero’s actions during the next turn. Permanent: The spell is permanent and never expires. Permanent spells can be in two states: active and inactive. When initially cast, the spell is active until the end of the action phase on the following turn.

title: Final Thoughts
content: Thank you for your support! In a game of this scope, there are bound to be oversights or errors. Please forgive me if I fell short of what you deserve as my customer. If a question arises during game play, make a fair judgment call and get back to the fun of the game. Later, check for an answer online or share your question so everyone can benefit. Most importantly, have FUN and make Dragons Down your own! Be sure to read aloud the story of your hero. “He was Boromin Longbow, human knight, redeemed outlaw, wielder of Decimation, wearer of the Elven Slippers and the Symbol of Stealth, Blood Offerer, slayer of the Great Drake and Orcs too many to count, deliverer of Food & Ale to the Keep, Spelunker, Bat Hawker, and Goblin Blight... became ogre soup on the 29th day of his arrival”. This game is dedicated to Richard Hamblen, the greatest board game designer in my view. He provided more joy to my childhood than he could possibly know.

title: Turn Start
content: • Clear all hidden, alert, sneak, and make noise statuses.

title: Actions
content: • Determine the active hero. • Active hero performs all of their actions. • Repeat until all heroes have taken a turn.

title: Monster Activation
content: • Roll the summoning dice. • Monsters may move and/or be summoned.

title: Combat
content: • Heroes cast spells and/or participate in combat.

title: MONSTER ACTIVATION
content: First player rolls the summoning dice. Monsters move and summon only in map tiles with heroes.

title: Wandering Monster Die (Gray)
content: 1. If an arrow, return all monsters in tiles without a hero to the monster tray. Monsters in tiles with heroes move to heroes. No monsters are summoned. 2. If die matches symbol on map tile, all monsters in tile move to heroes. 3. If die matches symbol on a map tile, wandering monsters are summoned.

title: Local Monster Die (Black)
content: 1. If die matches symbol on map tile, all monsters in tile move to heroes. 2. If die matches symbol on map tile, monster listed on map tile is summoned. 3. If die shows a site symbol, summon guardians to their treasure site.
